3735-the-inspector-general.title: The Inspector General
3735-the-inspector-general.creator: Nicolay Gogol
3735-the-inspector-general.description: A book by Nicolay Gogol. This unique character of Russian literature may be said to have had its beginning with the Inspector-General. Before Gogol most Russian writers, with few exceptions, were but weak imitators of foreign models. The drama fashioned itself chiefly upon French patterns. The Inspector-General and later Gogol's novel, Dead Souls, established that tradition in Russian letters which was followed by all the great writers from Dostoyevsky down to Gorky.

arxiv-2101-01042.title: Fast Ensemble Learning Using Adversarially-Generated Restricted Boltzmann Machines Journal: ArXiv
arxiv-2101-01042.creator: Gustavo H. de Rosa, Mateus Roder, João Paulo Papa
arxiv-2101-01042.description: Abstract Machine Learning has been applied in a wide range of tasks throughout the last years, ranging from image classification to autonomous driving and natural language processing. Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM) has received recent attention and relies on an energy-based structure to model data probability distributions. Notwithstanding, such a technique is susceptible to adversarial manipulation, i.e.

arxiv-2208-07914.title: PD-MORL: Preference-Driven Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
arxiv-2208-07914.creator: Toygun Basaklar, Suat Gumussoy, Umit Y. Ogras
arxiv-2208-07914.description: Abstract Multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) approaches have emerged to tackle many real-world problems with multiple conflicting objectives by maximizing a joint objective function weighted by a preference vector. These approaches find fixed customized policies corresponding to preference vectors specified during training . However, the design constraints and objectives typically change dynamically in real-life scenarios.

arxiv-2209-03227.title: Mixing time of random walk on dynamical random cluster
arxiv-2209-03227.creator: Andrea Lelli, Alexandre Stauffer
arxiv-2209-03227.description: Abstract We study the mixing time of a random walker who moves inside a dynamical random cluster model on the d d -dimensional torus of side-length n n . In this model, edges switch at rate μ \mu between open and closed , following a Glauber dynamics for the random cluster model with parameters p , q p,q .

arxiv-2304-13330.title: Recursive Quantum Eigenvalue/Singular-Value Transformation: Analytic Construction of Matrix Sign Function by Newton Iteration
arxiv-2304-13330.creator: Kaoru Mizuta, Keisuke Fujii
arxiv-2304-13330.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kaoru Mizuta, Keisuke Fujii. Quantum eigenvalue transformation (QET) and its generalization, quantum singular value transformation (QSVT), are versatile quantum algorithms that allow us to apply broad matrix functions to quantum states, which cover many of significant quantum algorithms such as Hamiltonian simulation. However, finding a parameter set which realizes preferable matrix functions in these techniques is difficult for large-scale quantum systems: there is no analytical result other than trivial cases as far as we know and we often suffer also from numerical instability.

arxiv-2305-11621.title: Positive Toeplitz Operators from a Weighted Harmonic Bloch Space into Another
arxiv-2305-11621.creator: Ömer Faruk Doğan
arxiv-2305-11621.description: Abstract . We define positive Toeplitz operators between weighted harmonic Bloch spaces b α ∞ b^{\infty}_{\alpha} on the unit ball of ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} for the full range of parameter α ∈ ℝ \alpha\in\mathbb{R} . We give characterizations of bounded and compact Toeplitz operators taking one weighted harmonic Bloch space into another in terms of Carleson and vanishing Carleson measures.

arxiv-2307-15704.title: A JWST/MIRI and NIRCam Analysis of the Young Stellar Object Population in the Spitzer I Region of NGC 6822 Facilities: JWST (MIRI, NIRCam) aplpy ( Robitaille 2019 ) , astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , image1overf.p
arxiv-2307-15704.creator: Laura Lenkić, Conor Nally, Olivia C. Jones, Martha L. Boyer, Patrick J. Kavanagh, Nolan Habel, Omnarayani Nayak, Alec S. Hirschauer, Margaret Meixner, B. A. Sargent, Tea Temim
arxiv-2307-15704.description: Abstract We present an imaging survey of the Spitzer I star-forming region in NGC 6822 conducted with the NIRCam and MIRI instruments onboard JWST . Located at a distance of 490 kpc, NGC 6822 is the nearest non-interacting low-metallicity ( ∼ \sim 0.2 Z ⊙ Z_{\odot} ) dwarf galaxy.

arxiv-2311-09458.title: Lexical Repetitions Lead to Rote Learning: Unveiling the Impact of Lexical Overlap in Train and Test Reference Summaries
arxiv-2311-09458.creator: Prafulla Kumar Choubey, Alexander R. Fabbri, Caiming Xiong, Chien-Sheng Wu
arxiv-2311-09458.description: Abstract Ideal summarization models should generalize to novel summary-worthy content without remembering reference training summaries by rote. However, a single average performance score on the entire test set is inadequate in determining such model competencies. We propose a fine-grained evaluation protocol by partitioning a test set based on the lexical similarity of reference test summaries with training summaries.

arxiv-2404-03174.title: A comparison between the deflection angles of massive and massless particles in the Shchwarzschild space-time and their consequences on black hole shadows
arxiv-2404-03174.creator: S. Mendoza, M. Santibañez
arxiv-2404-03174.description: Abstract We present comparisons of the deflection angles of massless and massive particles in the Schwarzschild space-time. For the case of photons in a general static space-time, we construct a spatial 3D equation of motion for their path that leads to an implicit formula for the deflection angle.

arxiv-2406-04003.description: Abstract Context. Since 2019, GRAVITY has provided direct observations of giant planets and brown dwarfs at separations of down to 95 mas from the host star. Some of these observations have provided the first direct confirmation of companions previously detected by indirect techniques (astrometry and radial velocities). Aims.

arxiv-2504-06019.title: Radiatively-Cooled Moist Convection under an Idealised Climate Change Scenario: Linear Analysis
arxiv-2504-06019.creator: G. N. Dritschel 1 ∗, S. M. Tobias 1, D. J. Parker 1,2,3 and L. Tomassini 4 1 School of Mathematics, University of Leeds, Leeds LS2 9JT, UK 2 NORCE Norwegian Research Centre AS, Bergen NO-5838, NO 3 National Centre for Atmospheric Science (NCAS), Leeds LS2 9JT 4 Met Office, Exeter EX1 3PB, UK
arxiv-2504-06019.description: Abstract In order to explore the effects of climate change on atmospheric convection and the water cycle, we develop and analyse an extension of the Rainy-Bénard model, which is itself a moist version of the Rayleigh-Bénard model of dry convection. Including moisture changes the character of the convection, with condensation providing a source of buoyancy via latent heating.

arxiv-2508-12829.title: Entropy-driven phase transition in a non-collinear antiferromagnet due to higher-order exchange interactions
arxiv-2508-12829.creator: Leo Kollwitz, Moritz A. Goerzen, Bjarne Beyer, Hendrik Schrautzer, Stefan Heinze
arxiv-2508-12829.description: Abstract The triple-Q state arises due to the superposition of three symmetry equivalent spin spirals stabilized by higher-order exchange interactions. It has been predicted more than 20 years ago but was only recently discovered in a Mn monolayer on the Re(0001) surface. To date little is known about the thermodynamic properties of this intriguing non-coplanar spin state.

arxiv-2601-10623.title: Fair Regression under Demographic Parity: A Unified Framework
arxiv-2601-10623.creator: Yongzhen FengCenter for Statistical Science, Tsinghua University, Weiwei WangDepartment of Statistics, Texas A&M University, Raymond K. W. WongDepartment of Statistics, Texas A&M Universityand, Xianyang ZhangDepartment of Statistics, Texas A&M University
arxiv-2601-10623.description: Abstract We propose a unified framework for fair regression tasks formulated as risk minimization problems subject to a demographic parity constraint. Unlike many existing approaches that are limited to specific loss functions or rely on challenging non-convex optimization, our framework is applicable to a broad spectrum of regression tasks.

bound-to-rise-or-up-the-ladder.title: Bound to Rise; Or, Up the Ladder
bound-to-rise-or-up-the-ladder.creator: Jr. Alger, Horatio

pmc-10496262.title: Prediction of diabetes disease using an ensemble of machine learning multi-classifier models
pmc-10496262.creator: Karlo Abnoosian, Rahman Farnoosh, Mohammad Hassan Behzadi
pmc-10496262.description: Background and objectiveDiabetes is a life-threatening chronic disease with a growing global prevalence, necessitating early diagnosis and treatment to prevent severe complications. Machine learning has emerged as a promising approach for diabetes diagnosis, but challenges such as limited labeled data, frequent missing values, and dataset imbalance hinder the development of accurate prediction models.

pmc-11367983.title: A Bayesian approach for estimating the uncertainty on the contribution of nitrogen fixation and calculation of nutrient balances in grain legumes
pmc-11367983.creator: Francisco Palmero, Trevor J. Hefley, Josefina Lacasa, Luiz Felipe Almeida, Ricardo J. Haro, Fernando O. Garcia, Fernando Salvagiotti, Ignacio A. Ciampitti
pmc-11367983.description: BackgroundThe proportion of nitrogen (N) derived from the atmosphere (Ndfa) is a fundamental component of the plant N demand in legume species. To estimate the N benefit of grain legumes for the subsequent crop in the rotation, a simplified N balance is frequently used. This balance is calculated as the difference between fixed N and removed N by grains.

pmc-11595838.title: Incorporation of Silver into Sulfate Groups Enhances Antimicrobial and Antiviral Effects of Fucoidan
pmc-11595838.creator: Akira Iwata, Mayuko Yamamoto-Fujimura, Suzuka Fujiwara, Saya Tajima, Takahide Shigeyama, Moriya Tsukimoto, Tatsuya Ibuki, Akito Kataoka-Kato, Adele Cutignano
pmc-11595838.description: The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly impacted our daily lives. Routine infection-control measures present an effective preventive strategy for a new infectious disease outbreak. Fucoidan, a fucose-rich sulfated polysaccharide found in brown algae, exhibits antiviral activity. Moreover, fucoidan exerts an antimicrobial effect; however, it requires considerably higher concentrations than those needed for its antiviral effect.

pmc-12525030.title: Atherosclerotic Plaque Crystals Induce Endothelial Dysfunction
pmc-12525030.creator: Jishamol Thazhathveettil, Sherin Aloysius Gomez, Deborah Olaoseeji, Rongrong Wu, Allan Sirsjö, Geena Varghese Paramel, Ida Daniela Perrotta
pmc-12525030.description: Endothelial dysfunction is an early driver of atherosclerosis, yet the direct impact of endogenous crystals such as cholesterol crystals and monosodium urate on endothelial activation remains incompletely understood. In this study, we examine how crystalline stimuli modulate human umbilical vein endothelial cells by assessing inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial respiration, and neutrophil recruitment.

pmc-12564947.title: Unsupervised Segmentation of Bolus and Residue in Videofluoroscopy Swallowing Studies
pmc-12564947.creator: Farnaz Khodami, Mehdy Dousty, James L. Coyle, Ervin Sejdić
pmc-12564947.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Bolus tracking is a critical component of swallowing analysis, as the speed, course, and integrity of bolus movement from the mouth to the stomach, along with the presence of residue, serve as key indicators of potential abnormalities. Existing machine learning approaches for videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS) analysis heavily rely on annotated data and often struggle to detect residue, which is visually subtle and underrepresented.

pmc-12581555.title: Symptom burden in middle-aged women, the role of immigrant status
pmc-12581555.creator: Nilam Shakeel, Anne Karen Jenum, Christin Wiegels Waage, Ibrahimu Mdala, Erik L. Werner, Bård Natvig, Anja Maria Braend
pmc-12581555.description: BackgroundSubjective health complaints (SHCs) are symptoms from various organs that do not have an obvious explanation. Immigrants in Western countries are often exposed to multiple stressors that may trigger SHCs. Increased symptom load may reflect subjective health and functioning in the present and in the future.

pmc-12704301.title: The spatio-functional cortical representation of muscles innervated by the accessory nerve using nTMS
pmc-12704301.creator: J Reinsch, M Denker, M Engelhardt, A Zdunczyk, D Huscher, P Vajkoczy, T Picht, NF Dengler
pmc-12704301.description: Highlights•nTMS mapping of cortical muscle areas in accessory nerve lesions vs. controls.•Sternocleidomastoideus and trapezius differed in cortical site, size and laterality.•Motor thresholds higher contralateral; SCM area smaller or absent post-transection.Keywords: nTMS, Accessory nerve, Cortical muscle representation, Sternocleidomastoid muscle, Trapezius muscle Introduction The accessory nerve innervates both the trapezius and sternocleidomastoid muscle.

pmc-12987162.title: A Resonator-Based Flexible Antenna for Non-Invasive Deep Brain Temperature Sensing with Microwave Radiometry †
pmc-12987162.creator: Golap Kanti Dey, Mohammad Vaseem, Natalia K. Nikolova, Atif Shamim, Chih-Hung Chen
pmc-12987162.description: We present a circular complementary split ring resonator (CCSRR) flexible antenna operating in the 1.4 GHz radio-astronomy quiet frequency band. The antenna is designed for microwave non-invasive brain temperature sensing of an infant’s head to aid in the therapeutic hypothermia treatment of hypoxic–ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) and traumatic brain injury (TBI).

pmc-13179030.title: Improving the First-hour Breastfeeding Rate in Cesarean Deliveries: A Quality Improvement Initiative
pmc-13179030.creator: Nalina Amuji, Clive Martin Rodrigues, Harshitha M. Swamy, Lakshmi Parvathi Bandlamudi, Tinu Krishna vilasam Regunath, Chandrakala Bada Shekharappa
pmc-13179030.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Introduction:Breastfeeding during the golden hour after birth is crucial for establishing successful long-term breastfeeding. Despite the World Health Organization recommendation, according to the National Family Health Survey-5, the first-hour breastfeeding rate in India following cesarean delivery is only 23.9%.

pmc-13285674.title: Naive CD4+ T cells synthesize a hyaluronan-rich glycocalyx that is diminished following activation

pmc-13658023.title: High sperm DNA fragmentation is associated with increased embryonic chromosomal abnormality: a retrospective study of 8 years involving 5637 couples undergoing ART
pmc-13658023.creator: Li Lou, Pengcheng Xu, Pingyuan Xie, Huan Zhang, Yifan Gu, Fei Gong, Ge Lin, Guangxiu Lu, Jing Dai, Shujuan Ma
pmc-13658023.description: STUDY QUESTIONDoes sperm DNA fragmentation impair blastocyst chromosomal integrity?SUMMARY ANSWERA high sperm DNA fragmentation index (DFI) is associated with an increased risk of blastocyst aneuploidy, particularly when the man has poor semen quality or when the female partner is aged ≥35 years.

pmc-13670528.title: Chemical prophage induction selectively removes Vibrio from a pelagic Sargassum-derived multispecies biofilm
pmc-13670528.creator: Alexandra K. Stiffler, Natascha S. Varona, Bailey A. Wallace, Cynthia B. Silveira
pmc-13670528.description: BackgroundPelagic Sargassum has undergone significant range expansion and dramatic blooms in the Atlantic over the past 15 years. This alga’s microbiome provides symbiotic functions that are believed to contribute to its ecological success. Recent research shows that Sargassum-associated bacteria are enriched in integrated prophages compared to the surrounding seawater and that these prophages are inducible by chemical and ultraviolet treatment.
